Package neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.seal

Class NeumannLabyrinthSolver

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.seal.NeumannLabyrinthSolver
final class NeumannLabyrinthSolver extends Object
Tooth-by-tooth (modified Neumann) labyrinth leakage solver used by LabyrinthSealFlowCalculator.

For a trial mass flow m the solver marches through the teeth. At tooth i, with upstream pressure p_i (Pa), gas density rho_i and real-gas isentropic exponent k_i, the downstream pressure solves 

 p_{i+1}^2 = p_i^2 - (m / (Cf_i u_i A))^2 p_i / rho_i
 Cf_i = pi / (pi + 2 - 5 beta_i + 2 beta_i^2),  beta_i = max((p_i / p_{i+1})^((k_i - 1) / k_i) - 1, 0)
 u_0 = 1,  u_i = sqrt(n / (n (1 - alpha) + alpha)),  alpha = 1 - 1 / (1 + 16.6 c / t)^2

The flow coefficient depends on p_{i+1}, so each tooth is solved for its pressure ratio with a bracketed Brent search between the critical ratio and 1, where the residual increases monotonically. The state after each tooth is an exact PH flash of the inlet gas at the inlet enthalpy. A tooth chokes when p_{i+1} would fall below p_i (2/(k_i + 1))^(k_i/(k_i - 1)). The leakage is the flow for which the pressure after the last tooth equals the outlet pressure (Brent root search). When that pressure cannot be reached without a tooth choking, the leakage is the largest flow at which no tooth chokes (the choked flow).

The march does not depend on the outlet pressure, so marches are cached per trial flow and reused across outlet pressures. GERG-2008 fluids with a single-phase gas inlet first try the dedicated PHflashGERG2008 and fall back to the general PHflash when the expanded state is multiphase or misses the inlet enthalpy; every other fluid uses the general PHflash. Every state is checked against the inlet enthalpy.

    • toothPressureRatio

      private static double toothPressureRatio(double k, double d)
      Solves the dimensionless tooth equation y^2 = 1 - d / Cf(y)^2 for the pressure ratio y = p_{i+1}/p_i, with Cf(y) = pi/(pi + 2 - 5 beta + 2 beta^2) and beta = max(y^(-(k-1)/k) - 1, 0).

      The residual y^2 - 1 + d/Cf(y)^2 increases monotonically between the critical ratio and 1 and is positive at 1, so the tooth chokes exactly when the residual at the critical ratio is not negative; otherwise the single root is found with a bracketed Brent search. A plain fixed-point iteration on this equation can oscillate for high k.

      Parameters:
      k - real-gas isentropic exponent upstream of the tooth
      d - dimensionless drop flux^2 / (p_i rho_i), with flux = m / (u_i A)
      Returns:
      pressure ratio y, or NaN when the tooth chokes

    • isenthalpicState

      private static double[] isenthalpicState(SystemInterface inletGas, double inletEnthalpy, boolean useGergFlash, double pressurePa, double warmStartK)
      Flashes the inlet gas to a pressure at the inlet enthalpy.

      The dedicated GERG-2008 PH flash only handles single-phase gas and returns after its TP flash otherwise, so when it finds more than one phase or misses the inlet enthalpy the general PH flash is used instead. Every state is checked against the inlet enthalpy.

      Parameters:
      inletGas - inlet gas template; it is cloned
      inletEnthalpy - inlet enthalpy in J (total for the system)
      useGergFlash - true to try the dedicated GERG-2008 PH flash first
      pressurePa - pressure in Pa
      warmStartK - initial temperature guess in K
      Returns:
      {temperature K, gas density kg/m3, gas real-gas isentropic exponent}
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the inlet enthalpy is not reached or no gas phase remains
